title: Filolial Producer
text: It’s been two days since we crossed the border. The frequency of assassin attacks has dropped dramatically. It seems operating outside Melromarc really was difficult after all. I suppose even those who are after my father can’t act so freely in other countries. After all, my father is the Shield Hero. From the window of the carriage, my father asks us:
“How long will it take to get to Siltvelt by carriage?”
“It’d take at least three weeks on horseback.”
“That’s pretty far, huh…”
“I hear Filolial-sama could make it in two weeks.”
“Is there really that much of a difference between Filolial-sama’s speed and a horse’s? If so, wouldn’t a flying dragon be faster?”

Éclair is spouting some outrageous nonsense. Dragons are Filolial-sama’s natural enemy—which means they’re my natural enemy, too. I can’t stand the thought of riding such a natural enemy. It makes my skin crawl. I’d rather crawl on the ground than do something like that.

Come to think of it, I haven’t seen Filolial-sama in quite a while. Well, I do catch glimpses of her as she passes by, but I haven’t actually touched her or smelled her. Ah… I’m dying to smell Filolial-sama’s scent. I pull a feather she shed—which had fallen to the ground—out of my pocket and hold it close to my nose. The lingering scent of Filolial-sama…
“I miss Filolial-sama so much.”
“Mo… Motoyasu-kun, you really do l-love Filolial-sama, don’t you?”
As we chatted like this while walking along the highway, a ranch came into view. Ah! It looks like a ranch that raises Filolial-sama! I lean over the fence and stare intently.
“Gua-gua!”
In the distance, Filolial-sama are relaxing carefree.
“Haa…”
“…So you really do love Filolial-sama that much, Lord Kitamura.”
“I wonder if Filolial-sama is for sale anywhere?”
My patience is finally reaching its limit. Filolial-sama! My body is itching to catch a whiff of her scent.
“Hmm, if you want her that badly, I suppose I have a little extra money to spare. Why not just buy some?”
“Is that really true!?”
“Ah, yes…”
Éclair said something wonderful. The envoy from Siltvelt is nodding as well, though with a somewhat troubled expression.
“That would be nice, but… well… I’m a little tired from this long carriage ride. After all, I’ve been doing nothing but resting in the carriage the whole time.”
“Now that we’ve made it this far, we probably don’t need to be too wary of pursuers. How about resting in a nearby town to restock supplies and let the Shield Hero get some rest?”
“Are you sure there’s no danger of assassins coming?”

The envoy from Siltvelt nodded in response to my question. It’s dangerous to let our guard down, but if we ruin our health, it’ll all be for nothing. Besides, my Father is still only Level 1. It might be better to level him up a bit, both for his health and his abilities.
“There’s a location where one of our country’s collaborators has a branch office. It should be safe there…”
“Understood. Then, I, Motoyasu, will go negotiate at Philorial Ranch to see if I can get an egg from Filolial-sama.”
“Wouldn’t one that’s already hatched be fine?”
“It’s better to raise one from an egg.”
“Is that so? Well, I can spare a little time, so maybe Motoyasu-kun could raise it?”
“Of course! I’ll make sure to raise it into a magnificent Filolial-sama. Well then, I’ll go buy one.”
I asked my Father and the others to wait, and I made my way alone toward the ranch’s management hut. I knocked on the door of the management hut. … There was no answer. Is no one home?
“Mr. Kitamura—”
I turned around at the sound of Éclair’s voice. Éclair then pointed toward the Filolial barn. Since the office was empty, it made sense to check there.
“Gua-gua.”
Drawn by the sound, I peered into the Filolial barn. There, a burly man who looked like a farmer was feeding straw to Filolial-sama. He must be the ranch owner.
“Who’s there?”
“A visitor.”
“You’re told ‘Who’s there’ and you answer ‘a visitor’… Well, fine. So? What does this visitor want?”
“I’d like to ask for one of the eggs that Filolial-sama is hatching.”
“You… do you even know what kind of ranch this is?”
The farmer asked me something. Hmm… I have absolutely no idea what he’s talking about.
“I don’t know. I just want Filolial-sama.”
I can’t stand it any longer. Holding the meat my Father gave me in one hand, I approach Filolial-sama.
“Stop it. I’m trying to manage her weight. Don’t give her any extra food.”
“Hmm…”
So how am I supposed to get close to Filolial-sama, then? Filolial-sama turns her curious eyes toward me. There are various ways to become friends from here on out, but first impressions are crucial.
“Anyway, I want Filolial-sama’s eggs.”
“That’s what I’ve been telling you—I can’t give you any of the Filolials from here. If you really want them, I’ll sell you eggs laid elsewhere.”
“I’m not picky. If you’re going to sell them, I’d like you to sell them to me as soon as possible, wouldn’t you agree?”
“Why do you want a Filolial so badly?”
Why? There’s no particular reason. I raise them simply because Filolial-sama exists. There’s no room for my brain to get involved in that. If I had to say, that’s just the way the world works.
“Because they’re irreplaceable and precious to me. Do you ask for a reason to breathe?”
“That doesn’t make any sense… You want them that badly, yet you don’t have any particular attachment to them?”
“I love Filolial-sama equally. Yes… just like my own children—whether they’re quick or slow, strong or weak, smart or silly—I love them all equally…”
The farmer has his pitchfork resting on his shoulder and looks utterly dumbfounded. Was there something so absurd about that?
“What’s so funny?”
“…Do you really like Filolial-sama?”
“Of course I do.”
“Then this breed of Filolial—”

“It’s the Philitelto breed, isn’t it? No, actually, it’s a cross with the Philobred breed. Going back even further, there’s the Fisaun breed… I suspect there’s some Fidermeo blood mixed in on the paternal side.”

All the Filolial-samas in this stable seem to have been bred with speed in mind… It looks like they’ve gathered the breeds commonly seen in the Filolial races at Zeltoble. This ranch appears to be dedicated to breeding Thoroughbreds. That likely explains the weight management I mentioned earlier.
“They’re fast, but they seem to have some issues with their legs. Rather than focusing on weight management, I think the priority should be ensuring proper nutrition to prevent injuries.”
If we were to purchase one, it would be quite expensive.
“Y-you’re right. To identify the bloodline at a glance—you’re quite the expert, aren’t you…”
“It’s only natural when it comes to love.”
Seeing the trust Filolial-sama placed in the farmer in his eyes, I found myself convinced as well. I gently placed my hand on his throat—a spot that always pleases Filolial-sama.
“Guaa…”
“Well now… We’ve just met, but you don’t seem like a bad guy.”
The farmer gave a sly grin. There are no villains among those who show such enthusiasm for Filolial-sama. I returned the smile.

Ah, Filolial-sama… By the way, Filolial-sama belongs to a species whose appearance changes significantly due to both innate lineage and acquired growth. While the lineages of Ku, Marin, and Midori are each based on species suited for combat, the fact that their specialties differed as they grew up is related to their acquired development.

Kuu and Marin possessed characteristics unique to their species—such as breathing fire or excelling at Magic—but Midori, who is naturally adept at poison and corruption, became skilled in close combat due to her environment. In line with that, her height also increased in her Filolial King form. Although she disliked it, she is taller than the average for her species.

My Father said that Filo-tan is an average Filolial. However, she possesses traits that would be impossible for an ordinary Filolial. Whether that’s due to genetics or the environment, even I can’t say for sure. Depending on how she’s raised, she can embody a wide range of possibilities. That’s one of the fascinating characteristics of Filolial-sama.
“Whether they’re cheap or expensive, I’ll cherish every Filolial-sama equally… that’s all there is to it.”
“I don’t really get it, but I see your enthusiasm. I don’t even know your name, but I’ll give you one really good one as a special favor.”
“Not just one—please tell me where else I can buy eggs, even if they’re cheap.”
“How many do you plan to raise?!”
“I want to raise every single Filolial-sama I can possibly handle!”
The farmer is clutching his head in exasperation.
“I don’t know what’s going on, but you’re fine with them being cheap, right?”
“I do not judge their worth based on values set by others.”
“I don’t quite get what you’re saying, but I get your enthusiasm. You’re an interesting one. How much money do you have?”

I show the farmer the money I have on me. Since I didn’t get any from those Trashes this time, I don’t have that much money. However, I do have the money I looted from the Melromarc soldiers and assassins I defeated along the way. This should be enough to buy a few eggs.
“I’d like you to pick out some Filolial-sama eggs that I can buy with this.”
“Well then…”
The farmer checks the money bag and nods a few times.
“I’ll give you one particularly good one, and as a bonus, I’ll throw in two more. Is that okay?”
“Understood!”

And so, guided by the farmer, I was led to a nearby warehouse where Filolial-sama’s eggs were stored. Then, the farmer brought out one egg from the back—as if it were his prized possession—and the two bonus eggs from the front.

“I’ll sell them to you along with the incubator. Take good care of them. The other cheap ones are meant to be sold to monster merchants. Since I’m in charge of selling eggs in this area, you were lucky to come to me first.”
“I’m grateful!”
“Come show them to me when you have time.”
“Got it! I’ll come show you these little ones once they’ve grown into the legendary Filolial-sama!”
And so, I purchased three Filolial eggs from the farmer. Alright, I like it here. I’ll make sure to save this portal.

Incidentally, as I later learned, the farmer at this ranch was apparently a major landowner of Filolial ranches in this area. Shipping Filolials to all sorts of places—he’s truly a model Filolial producer!
